title: Console UI & Rollouts — Weekly notes
body:
Week: 2026-03-09 — 2026-03-12
Owner: Maya Chen (eng-console-tooling)
Purpose: Capture weekly standup-style updates focused on Console UI changes, rollout progress and analytics/telemetry gaps. This doc is a lightweight working notes file for triage and async review (not the final launch brief).

SUMMARY
- Focus this week: finish canary automation for the modular rollouts UI, stabilize rollout rollback path, add missing telemetry for feature-flag exposure and per-route latency.
- Outcome: Canary automation merged to staging; observed 6% median latency increase on stressed machines (investigation in progress).

DETAILED UPDATES
1) UI / Frontend
- What shipped: modular rollouts page (iteration 1) merged behind flag ff:rollouts-modular-panel. PR 421 contains most changes; Diego addressed the main accessibility comments.
- Remaining work:
  - Final CSS polish for narrow viewports (Ravi) — 2d
  - Keyboard navigation gaps for the rollout list — ticket CT-241
  - Add rollout status badges to the route list (design already approved) — blocked on a small API change (see Rollouts/API).
- Notes: We intentionally left the inline analytics toggle off for canary users until we validate event volume.

2) Rollouts / Backend & Automation
- Canary automation: A small k8s job plus a controller that flips FF for 5% -> 25% -> 100% based on SLO metrics. Merged to staging; runs via pipeline 'rollout-canary-v2'.
- Observed behavior: When moving from 5% to 25% on the internal staging cluster, we saw a spike in p95 for the route-resolution RPC. Root cause candidate: badge rendering causes extra server-side calls for batch route metadata.
- Immediate mitigations:
  - Short-term: revert metadata prefetch in controller for flagged users (feature toggle) — Benji on it, due 2026-03-13.
  - Mid-term: change metadata prefetch to lazy fetch with caching (engineering spike 2d).
- Rollback path: Verified automatic rollback triggers on sustained p95 > 300ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows. Test run simulated failure and rollback worked end-to-end.

3) Analytics / Telemetry
- Gaps discovered:
  - No reliable event for "rollout-exposed" with variant id; current event only logs route/flag name (CT-250).
  - Latency attribution: tokens are tagged with model & region, but not with front-end route id; need to add route_id in traces so Console can show model-serving latency broken down by console route.
- Dashboards: Updated console-metrics-v2 to include a "rollout canary" panel (p50/p95, error-rate, and a small histogram of CPU utilization for affected nodes). Saved on dashboard path.
- Data volume: Initial canary at 5% is expected to increase events by ~0.7k/day; 25% would be ~3.5k/day — we validated ingestion limits and retention is fine for now.

BLOCKERS / RISKS
- Blocker: API change needed to include route metadata in the rollouts list endpoint. Without it, the UI must make an additional call per row which spikes backend load (ticket CT-246). Blocker owner: Ravi.
- Risk: If we push to 25% without lazy prefetch, p95 may exceed the rollback threshold in production. Recommendation: hold at 5% until lazy prefetch is implemented.
- Compliance: No PII observed in telemetry, but double-checked instrumentation to ensure no query strings or customer tokens are emitted.

DECISIONS MADE
- Hold 25% expansion until metadata prefetch is converted to lazy cached fetch (decision made 2026-03-11 during triage).
- Enable automated rollback on p95 > 300ms for 3 windows (conservative threshold for initial canary).

NEXT WEEK PRIORITIES (2026-03-16 sprint start)
- Implement lazy metadata prefetch (Ravi) — target complete by 2026-03-15.
- Add rollout-exposed event with variant ID and route_id (Sofia + analytics) — CT-250.
- Finish keyboard accessibility fixes (Diego) — CT-241.
- Run a controlled canary to 25% on staging with simulated load (Benji to run harness) — aim for 2026-03-16.
- Prepare a short playbook for oncall to handle rollback scenarios (SRE/Benji) — draft by 2026-03-14.

ACTION ITEMS (owner / due)
- Ravi: unblock API change CT-246 and submit API contract PR (due 2026-03-13).
- Benji: implement temporary revert to stop prefetch during canary and run rollback smoke test (due 2026-03-13).
- Sofia: add event schema and telemetry pipeline config for rollout-exposed event (CT-250) (due 2026-03-15).
- Diego: accessibility fixes and QA signoff for modular panel (due 2026-03-15).
- Maya: update canary runbook and coordinate with SRE for staging load test (due 2026-03-14).

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO PM
- PM ask: Are we comfortable showing partial rollout badges to users before the analytics toggle is enabled? Suggestion: show UI badge but hide exposure counts until telemetry is fully in place.
- Product: Need to confirm whether variant labels will be user-friendly strings or stable IDs (affects telemetry design).

MEETING LOG / ATTENDEES (triage 2026-03-11)
- Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Martinez, Ravi Kumar, Sofia Lopez, Benji O'Connor, Aaron Li (SRE), Priya Shah (PM).
- Quick notes: Aaron recommended lowering canary expansion speed; Priya approved holding at 5% until lazy fetch ready.

RELATED LINKS
- Rollout plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CT/console-rollout-plan
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/421
- Tickets: CT-234, CT-241, CT-246, CT-250

-- end of notes --
